body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{jh}(w)=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{j,T_j+h}-\sum_{i\in D_{jh}}w_{jh,i}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,T_j+h}\), with honest-width frontier \(W_s\) and fixed-Bonferroni SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\) for \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\)

sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed integer dimensions, deterministic adoption dates, rational predictors and class radii, a known rational covariance factor, and a certified rational Bonferroni multiplier.
sampling_model.units: The finite set \(\mathcal I\) contains treated, not-yet-treated, and never-treated units; repeated unit--calendar-time cells are deduplicated in \(Q\).
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and deterministic; \(D_{jh}=\{i:T_i>T_j+h\}\) identifies untreated donor outcomes at the relevant calendar time.
sampling_model.overlap: Every deepest donor pool \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty, which also makes every nested donor pool feasible.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no random nuisance estimation: weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design and model inputs, and correlated Gaussian-max calibration is reserved for a post-solve refinement.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper uses a common deepest-horizon donor pool while identifying the underlying shrinking donor-set geometry.
The paper offers non-asymptotic staggered synthetic-control prediction intervals, conic implementations, and uniform inference across post-treatment periods.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for scalar linear functionals over convex regression classes under known-variance Gaussian errors.
The paper trades worst-case conditional imbalance against variance when constructing generalized optimal matching weights.
The paper constructs facial-reduced extended duals with strong duality when ordinary conic constraint qualifications fail.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient closed-cone conditions for Farkas lemmas and strong duality in second-order-cone programming.

body.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking sets of not-yet-treated donors. Conditional on a rationally encoded fixed design, the proposal turns all treated-unit--horizon errors into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector, derives the exact worst-case bias radius, and chooses horizon-specific simplex weights by a rational fixed-Bonferroni SOCP. The band is finite-sample honest and lies within a dimension-uniform factor of the best deterministic linear synthetic-control rectangle. A concrete two-horizon staggered instance has an outward-rounded positive \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\) interval, and the open theorem-level step is a finite algebraic iff certificate for strict SOCP improvement that remains complete on degenerate active faces. Feasible-set inclusion is retained only as a boundary check. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein supply the published shrinking-pool support geometry, not a directly compared estimator.

project_justification.gap: BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 is the published anchor for horizon-varying donor eligibility and a common deepest support; the proposal does not claim that its two \(\Gamma\) programs evaluate or dominate that paper's partially pooled estimator. CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 supplies non-asymptotic simultaneous prediction intervals and conic implementations, but does not minimize honest joint width over horizon-specific donor simplexes. Scalar convex-class efficiency theory does not supply the Gaussian-rectangle lower bound or a degeneracy-safe comparison of two nested conic feasible sets.
project_justification.niche: Known covariance with a prespecified spectral band, rational fixed inputs, and a bounded linear conditional-mean class isolate a finite-sample panel decision problem in which donor availability, worst-case bias, shared-cell covariance, multiplicity, and exact certification are visible. The target is the attainable honest-width frontier and an auditable test of when a common deepest-pool restriction is strictly costly for the SOCP objective.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a deduplicated contrast representation, an exact support-function bias radius, a finite-sample honest SOCP band, and a dimension-uniform width comparison. It gives an interval-certified staggered witness and poses a representation-complete facial-reduction certificate with explicit conic feasibility, exact algebraic verification, and a separation-dependent bit bound.

body.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2, paragraphs defining \(\mathcal D_{jk}\)) provide the shrinking-donor-set and fixed-support geometry anchor; no theorem here compares the proposed rule with their partially pooled estimator, and the weak feasible-set inclusion is only a boundary check. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; the frontier is informed by that machinery but changes the decision variable and loss. Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class; the lower comparison here concerns a rectangle of contrasts on different nested simplex faces. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, Theorems 2 and 3) and Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) provide Gaussian comparison and symmetric-convex-set tools for the correlation sandwich; the global spectral covariance band is instead an explicit restriction of this finite experiment with prespecified sensitivity calibration. Pataki (2013, Sections 3--4) and Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1) inform the facial-reduction and closed-cone ingredients, while the exact finite certificate and bit bound remain the open contribution. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) and Cao, Lu, and Wu (2026) study different prediction and long-panel inferential regimes. Cerulli (2024) selects donor counts for prediction error, not simultaneous honest width. Wei, Park, Kalangi, and Huang (2026) use placebo-in-time bootstrap calibration in a different regime.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact robust frontier \(W_s\) and the implementable SOCP frontier \(\Gamma_s\) are distinct objects. The primal--facial-dual strict-gap certificate and the concrete strict witness concern \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\); a strict SOCP gap alone does not prove \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}<W_{\mathrm{deep}}\). Correlated Gaussian-max calibration is a post-solve refinement and is not used to define the conic certificate.
body.honest_scope: Finite-sample coverage, the contrast-geometry sandwich, the constant-factor frontier, and the explicit two-horizon \(\Gamma\)-gap witness are theorem-level targets. Weak nested-support dominance is only the sanity proposition \texttt{prop:nested-support-boundary} and carries no novelty claim. The complete finite certificate on degenerate faces is exposed as \texttt{oeq:degenerate-iff-certificate}. The covariance band is a prespecified regularity restriction for the known-covariance finite experiment, with sensitivity calibration over its endpoints. Unknown covariance, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, and a direct comparison with the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein partially pooled estimator are outside this version. When donor sets coincide, the proposal reduces exactly to the fixed-pool problem; with one unbiased contrast, it reduces to a rationally certified classical known-covariance Gaussian interval.
